There's an old saying in the martial world: One sip of the Parting Tears, and even immortals hold no allure. Heroes from every corner of the Central Plains cherish this drink, and Heaven's Pier is famed for it. Yet most only taste a hint of its flavor, never grasping the true meaning behind "Parting Tears", nor what it means to be the one who parts. 
Some say the name speaks of sorrowful partings at Baling Bridge. Others believe it echoes the longing of lovers separated beneath the wandering moon. 
But only those in Heaven's Pier who've bargained with the Water Lady know the truth: the one who parts is always themselves. From that moment on, they leave the mortal world behind, and all they once held dear.

4806569047259750314:
Once, a blind musical duo perceived the world through melody, discerning colors by sound and mastering sonic combat. Legends say their music made plum blossoms shed snow, releasing sudden fragrance—hence their epithet.
During a Chang'an snowfall, they played beneath a plum tree, joined by a flutist who harmonized without words—a meeting of souls in notes.
Together, they composed "Winter’s Trio" celebrating pine, bamboo, and plum. While pine and bamboo were completed, the plum movement remained unfinished—a lasting regret.
Now, the musicians are gone, leaving only echoes of their art.
